neighbours.label: ' my' or ' our' opening a vocative address mid-sentence (', my friends,' / ', my lord,'), not an ordinary possessive
fire: I tell you truly, my brothers, that the harvest will fail this year.
Forgive me, my lord, but the messenger has not returned.
We have come a long way together, my comrades, and the end is near.
Do not weep, my children, for I shall return in the spring.
Pray tell, my good sir, what brings you to this village?
Remember, our beloved brethren, that patience is a virtue.
The night is cold, my friends, so gather close to the fire.
Behold, my people, the walls of the city have fallen.
quiet: I told my brothers that the harvest would fail this year.
Forgive me, lord, but the messenger has not returned.
We have come a long way together, comrades, and the end is near.
The children wept when my ship left harbour in the spring.
Pray tell, good sir, what brings you to this village?
Remember that our brethren in the north need patience.
The night is cold, so my friends gathered close to the fire.
Behold the walls of my city, which have fallen at last.

notes: Card: top 32 peak on ' my' (x20) and ' our' in direct address ('Consider, my brethren'). Probe: vocative 'my friends' 0.44, 'my lady' 0.30, 'our Father' 0.29, but 'my dear' only 0.07; plain possessive 'my umbrella'/'my kitchen' <0.01; the same vocative without 'my' 0.01.
